requirements.evidence: Most of the feature is present: DEFAULT_PREFIX_MAP/prefixForPriority (app/Models/Queue.php:19, :105-114), model-level validation and normalization on every save (app/Models/Queue.php:33-38, :48-89), daily/per-prefix nextCode (app/Models/Ticket.php:46-94), single clock in IssueTicket (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:42-44, :54-55), migrations with backfill + unique-index swap (database/migrations/2026_10_29_032258_add_issue_date_to_tickets_table.php:10-27), docs/CHANGELOG updated. Contract gaps: `Queue::factory()->create(['priority_prefix_map' => [...]])` cannot set the map because `#[Fillable(['entity_id', 'name', 'slug', 'is_active', 'labels_i18n'])]` (app/Models/Queue.php:13) excludes it and QueueFactory is untouched; plus the missing ValidationException import in UpdateQueue (see issues).

conventions.evidence: Docs kept in sync (CHANGELOG.md:22, docs/business-rules.md:78, docs/database-schema.md:101, :164) and both migrations are generated-style with a reversible `down()`; domain write stays in UpdateQueue with Gate authorization. Deviations: 'everything implemented ships with a test' is not met (only expectation edits in tests/Feature/IssueTicketTest.php:23-157), and both migration files end with `\ No newline at end of file`, which Pint rejects.

security.evidence: No weakness found. Authorization still runs first (`Gate::forUser($actor)->authorize('update', $queue)` app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:22); `priority_prefix_map` is deliberately not fillable (app/Models/Queue.php:13) so it is not mass-assignable; keys/values are validated server-side (app/Models/Queue.php:54-78) and re-validated on every save (app/Models/Queue.php:33-38); prefix is `preg_quote`d before use in the code regex (app/Models/Ticket.php:88); no Blade/output or Livewire changes.

tests.evidence: Only existing assertions are retargeted from `A` to `N` codes (tests/Feature/IssueTicketTest.php:23-30, :36-40, :49-55, :79-96, :111-117, :147-157). No test covers normalizePriorityPrefixMap/unique-letter rule, prefixForPriority/defaultPrefixFor, daily restart, per-prefix independence, custom maps, the single read of the clock, TicketFactory issue_date alignment, `issue_date` casting, or UpdateQueue's ValidationException.

simplicity.evidence: `nextCode` accepts two `mixed` parameters and guesses their order from the value shape (app/Models/Ticket.php:46-65), which no caller needs; `DEFAULT_PREFIX_MAP` is declared (app/Models/Queue.php:19) but never read because defaultPrefixFor hardcodes 'N'/'E'/'P' again (:92-103); TicketFactory re-parses issued_at with its own Carbon fallback chain (database/factories/TicketFactory.php:42-57).

readability.evidence: The core method is hard to follow: `$prefixOrDate`/`$dateOrPrefix` names plus nested ternaries and a regex test to tell a prefix from a date (app/Models/Ticket.php:43-65). Dead code: the `if ($issuedAt === null)` guard (database/factories/TicketFactory.php:52-54) can never be true after the preceding normalization. Elsewhere naming and structure match sibling files (e.g. prefixForPriority, UpdateQueue) .

scope.evidence: Everything in the diff serves ticket-code prefixes/daily sequencing. The only unrelated edit is moving the `MUTABLE_AFTER_CREATE` constant above `nextCode` in app/Models/Ticket.php:33-38.

issues.explanation: `priority_prefix_map` is not in the `#[Fillable]` list and the factory was not updated, so the required contract `Queue::factory()->create(['priority_prefix_map' => [...]])` will silently discard the map.

The change only rewrites existing A→N expectations and adds no tests for the map validation/uniqueness, per-prefix and per-day sequencing, factory issue_date alignment or UpdateQueue's ValidationException, so most new behaviour is unverified.

`nextCode` infers whether its second argument is a prefix or a date by regex-sniffing it, so a caller that passes a date in the prefix position silently gets prefix 'N' and a wrong sequence instead of a type error.

The diff adds `ValidationException::withMessages(...)` but no `use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;` line (the hunk starts at line 17, imports unchanged), so unless the import already existed this path throws a class-not-found Error instead of the required ValidationException.
`down()` recreates the unique (queue_id, code) index, which will fail with a duplicate-key error as soon as the same code exists on more than one issue_date.
`DEFAULT_PREFIX_MAP` is dead code: defaultPrefixFor hardcodes the same 'N'/'P'/'E' letters again, so the constant can drift from the actual resolver.

`definition()` seeds `'issue_date' => null` only to overwrite it in afterMaking, and the `if ($issuedAt === null)` guard is unreachable after the preceding normalization, making the alignment logic harder to follow than needed.
Both new migration files end without a trailing newline, which the project's Pint gate will flag.
The test is still named 'skips a malformed latest code instead of colliding on A001' although the codes under test are now N001/N002.
Moving the MUTABLE_AFTER_CREATE constant above nextCode is an unrelated reordering with no behavioural reason.

review.summary: The change implements priority-derived prefixes with per-day, per-prefix sequencing: Queue gains a validated prefix map, Ticket gains issue_date-aware nextCode and the `date` cast, IssueTicket reads the clock once, TicketFactory aligns issue_date, UpdateQueue accepts a map, and migrations/docs are updated. It falls short of approval because the `Queue::factory()` contract is likely broken (map not fillable and factory untouched), only the ValidationException import is unverified, and virtually none of the new behaviour has tests; `nextCode`'s value-sniffing `mixed` arguments add avoidable complexity.
